title: HTTP caching in 60 seconds
caption: HTTP caching in 60 seconds: the headers that decide whether your browser downloads a file again or not.

scenes.say: Every page needs the same logo, styles and scripts. Downloading them every time is slow. Caching keeps a copy.

scenes.code:
Cache-Control: max-age=31536000, immutable

Cache-Control: no-cache
ETag: "a1b2c3"
scenes.say: The server decides with headers. Max age says keep this for a year, no questions asked.
There are two ways to reuse a copy.

items.title: Fresh
items.text: use it, no request at all
items.say: If it's still fresh, the browser doesn't even ask.

items.title: Revalidate
items.say: If not, it asks whether the file changed, using the E tag.
And the server answers three oh four: not modified, keep yours.

scenes.text:
The fastest request
*is the one you never make.*
scenes.say: That's HTTP caching. The fastest request is the one you never make.
